parts.label: (a)(ii)
parts.text: State what is meant by *gravitational potential energy*.

parts.label: (b)
parts.part_stem:
An aircraft of mass $1200\text{ kg}$ climbs upwards with a constant velocity of $45\text{ m s}^{-1}$, as shown in Fig. 3.1.

{{figure:figure_3_1}}

Fig. 3.1 (not to scale)

The aircraft's engine produces a thrust force of $2.0 \times 10^3\text{ N}$ to move the aircraft through the air. The rate of increase in height of the aircraft is $3.3\text{ m s}^{-1}$.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.text: Calculate the power produced by the thrust force.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.part_stem: Determine, for a time interval of $3.0$ minutes,

parts.label: (b)(ii)1
parts.text: 1. the work done by the thrust force to move the aircraft,

parts.label: (b)(ii)2
parts.text: 2. the increase in gravitational potential energy of the aircraft,

parts.label: (b)(ii)3
parts.text: 3. the work done against air resistance.

parts.label: (b)(iii)
parts.text: Use your answer in (b)(ii) part 3 to calculate the force due to air resistance acting on the aircraft.

parts.label: (b)(iv)
parts.text: With reference to the motion of the aircraft, state and explain whether the aircraft is in equilibrium.
